did_you_know.text: Did you know? Boaz is described in the chapter as “a man of standing,” and he was a relative of Elimelech, Naomi’s deceased husband.
Did you know? Ruth happened to come to Boaz’s field, and the text describes it with the words, “As it happened, she came.”
Did you know? Boaz greeted the harvesters with the blessing, “The LORD be with you,” and they replied, “The LORD bless you.”
Did you know? The overseer of the harvesters told Boaz that Ruth was a Moabite girl who had returned with Naomi and that she had hardly stopped gleaning since morning.
Did you know? Boaz took care of Ruth’s safety: he ordered the young men not to touch her and allowed her to drink from the water the harvesters had drawn.
Did you know? Boaz praised Ruth for her loyalty to Naomi and for leaving her family and homeland, and he blessed her that the LORD would reward her for what she had done.
Did you know? During the meal, Boaz invited Ruth to eat with the harvesters. She ate her fill and even had some food left over.
Did you know? Boaz instructed his men to deliberately leave stalks of grain for Ruth, so she could glean without being rebuked or humiliated.
Did you know? After a day of gleaning, Ruth threshed what she had gathered, and it amounted to about an ephah of barley.
Did you know? When Naomi heard that Boaz had helped Ruth, she identified him as a relative and as one of the family’s potential redeemers.
